You are shown a snapshot of US macroeconomic and market data as it was known at the end of one month between 2007 and 2026.

Estimate which month the snapshot describes. Use only the figures supplied plus your general knowledge of economic history.

Reply with one JSON object and nothing else:
{"year": yyyy, "month": m, "confidence": c, "cues": ["...", "..."]}
Rules: year is an integer from 2007 to 2026; month is an integer from 1 to 12; c in [0, 1] is your confidence that the guess is within 6 months of the truth; 1 to 3 short cues citing the inputs.
text:
The pattern fits a period when policy rates had risen sharply over the prior 12 months, the 2-year yield was high, and the curve was inverted. Core CPI was low versus its own history while headline CPI was high, and payroll growth was weak relative to the past 3 years. Equities were doing well with low volatility, and the dollar was weak relative to its range.

Two windows fit this set: 2006-07 and 2022-23 or later. Since the data start in 2007, 2006-07 is out. The policy rate z-score of +2.0 with a 12m change of +2.0 suggests hikes within the last year, so I looked at 2023 and 2024.

Late 2023 doesn't fit well, because core CPI would still have been high versus its 3-year range. The core CPI 12m change of -2.0 does fit 2023-24, but the core level at -1.0 and headline at +1.5 is odd. Headline CPI rising by 1.0 over 3 months points to an energy spike.

The 36-month window for 2007-2008 would cover 2004-2007. Policy rate hikes ran from 2004 to mid-2006, so the 12m change would not be +2.0 in 2007. A 12m rise in the 2-year yield of +2.0 also fits 2005-06 better than 2007, so that window is out.

Another candidate is 2018, when the policy rate was rising, but its 36-month window began from the low-rate period, which fits a high policy rate z-score. In 2018 the unemployment rate was low and falling (-0.5 on 3m), and payrolls were weak relative to the past. Headline CPI rose in early 2018. VIX was low in 2018 but it spiked in February. Equity vol at -1.5 and 12m returns of +1.5 suggest roughly mid-2018 or late 2017. In 2018 the 10-year minus 2-year spread was flattening, and the dollar was weak in early 2018. Core CPI at -1.0 relative to the 2015-17 range is plausible. Credit spreads were tight. The 12m change in the dollar of -0.5 and the level of -1.5 suggest early 2018. Payrolls at -2.5 would be odd for 2018, though, unless it is a hurricane-affected month: September-October 2017 payrolls were hit by hurricanes. The 2-year yield was up 1.0 over 3m, which fits Dec 2017 to Jan 2018, and headline CPI rising fits as well. Equities had 1m, 3m and 6m gains with low vol, consistent with Jan 2018 or Dec 2017. Payrolls averaged weak in Oct 2017, which drags on the 3m average through November-December. The 10-year yield had a 3m change of 0.0 and the 2-year yield +1.0, so I'll pick Dec 2017.
